newsitem.title: USA: US MMS to set rule on oil/gas lease operations.
newsitem.headline: US MMS to set rule on oil/gas lease operations.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Friday it will publish a final rule to allow holders of offshore natural gas and oil leases 180 days between operations for leases continued beyond their primary terms, extending that duration from 90 days.
The MMS also said it will publish a rule continuing a requirement to begin exploratory drilling within five years on eight-year term leases.

The agency said the rule change increasing time between operations recognizes that the industry is focusing efforts in deeper waters, on subsalt projects, and in other areas of complex geology that require more time.

The MMS said it had considered removing the requirement to begin exploratory drilling within five years on leases with an eight-year term, but independent oil companies and drilling contractors said that provision was "necessary to ensure diligence."
